# Robot Vision and Learning Lab (RVL), University of Toronto

> Welcome to the Robot Vision and Learning (RVL) lab. We are part of the Computer Science department at the University of Toronto, the MCS department at UTM, the UofT Robotics Institute, and Vector Institute. The group is led by Prof. Florian Shkurti, and consists of students with backgrounds in robotics, machine learning, computer vision, engineering, control theory, or physics. We develop methods that enable robots to perceive, reason, and act effectively and safely, particularly in dynamic environments and alongside humans. Application areas include robotic manipulation, chemistry/biology lab automation, and field robotics for environmental monitoring.

## Pages

- [Home](https://rvl.cs.toronto.edu/): The Robot Vision and Learning (RVL) lab at the University of Toronto, led by Prof. Florian Shkurti, develops methods that let robots perceive, reason, and act effectively and safely.
- [Publications](https://rvl.cs.toronto.edu/publications/): Papers from the Robot Vision and Learning lab at the University of Toronto: robot learning, planning, 3D perception, lab automation, and field robotics.
- [Team](https://rvl.cs.toronto.edu/team/): Faculty, postdocs, graduate and undergraduate students, visitors, and alumni of the Robot Vision and Learning lab at the University of Toronto.
- [Research](https://rvl.cs.toronto.edu/research/): Research areas of the Robot Vision and Learning lab: reasoning and learning for robotics, safe robot learning, 3D vision and generative models, lab automation, and field robotics.
- [Joining](https://rvl.cs.toronto.edu/joining/): Information and FAQs for prospective postdocs, MSc and PhD students, undergraduates, and visiting students interested in the Robot Vision and Learning lab.
- [Blog](https://rvl.cs.toronto.edu/blog/): Blog posts from the Robot Vision and Learning lab at the University of Toronto.

## Research areas

- [Reasoning and learning for robotics](https://rvl.cs.toronto.edu/research/reasoning-and-learning-for-robotics/)
- [Safe robot learning](https://rvl.cs.toronto.edu/research/safe-robot-learning/)
- [3D vision and generative models for simulation](https://rvl.cs.toronto.edu/research/generative-models-and-perception/)
- [Robotics for chemistry and biology lab automation](https://rvl.cs.toronto.edu/research/robotics-for-chemistry-and-biology-lab-automation/)
- [Field robotics & environmental monitoring](https://rvl.cs.toronto.edu/research/field-robotics/)
